papers.title: ENHANCED TRIBOLOGICAL, MECHANICAL AND CORROSION PERFORMANCE OF MO AND NICR COATINGS ON LMD TI6AL4V ALLOY DEPOSITED VIA ATMOSPHERIC PLASMA SPRAYING IN A SELF -GOVERNMENT- DEVELOPED TECHNOLOGIES
papers.abstract: In this study, Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) alloy components were fabricated via Laser Metal Deposition (LMD) and subsequently coated with Nickel-Chromium (NiCr 80/20) and Molybdenum (Mo) powders using Atmospheric Plasma Spray (APS) to enhance their surface durability. The objective was to evaluate the synergistic effects of LMD and plasma spray coatings on the mechanical, tribological and corrosion properties of the Ti alloy. Microstructural and chemical analyses using SEM and EDS confirmed dense, uniform coatings with strong metallurgical bonding and minimal porosity. Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) revealed refined surface topographies, with Mo-coated samples exhibiting smoother profiles (Ra = 0.42 µm) compared to NiCr (Ra = 0.51 µm), facilitating better tribological contact. Vickers microhardness tests indicated significant surface strengthening, with hardness values increasing from 368 HV (uncoated) to 584.67 HV (Mo) and 537.66 HV (NiCr). Dry sliding wear tests demonstrated that Mo coatings provided superior wear resistance, with the lowest coefficient of friction (0.32) and specific wear rate (0.5 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/Nm), attributed to the formation of MoO₃ tribolayers. Electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5% NaCl solution revealed that NiCr coatings outperformed Mo in corrosion protection, exhibiting a more noble corrosion potential (–450 mV) and significantly reduced current density (1.2 × 10⁻⁷ mA/cm²) due to the formation of a stable Cr₂O₃ passive film. These findings establish that integrating LMD with tailored plasma spray coatings enables surface-functionalized Ti alloys suitable for high-performance applications requiring enhanced wear and corrosion resistance.
papers.venue: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文重点在于LMD制备Ti-6Al-4V后进行等离子喷涂涂层以增强表面性能，未涉及基体力学或疲劳性能，不符合L1方向要求。
llm.why_not_core: Paper focuses on plasma-sprayed coatings for surface enhancement, not on base mechanical/fatigue behavior of as-built Ti-6Al-4V; no tensile, fatigue, or anisotropy data; process is LMD, not LPBF/SLM/EBM/DED.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过LMD制备Ti-6Al-4V合金并喷涂Mo和NiCr涂层以提高其表面耐久性。
summary_zh.method: 采用大气等离子喷涂在LMD Ti-6Al-4V上沉积Mo和NiCr涂层，进行微观结构、硬度、磨损和腐蚀测试。
summary_zh.result: Mo涂层磨损率最低（0.5×10⁻⁴ mm³/Nm），NiCr涂层腐蚀防护最佳（-450 mV）。
summary_zh.validation: 通过SEM、EDS、AFM、硬度、磨损和电化学腐蚀测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the surface durability of LMD-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V alloy by applying Mo and NiCr coatings via atmospheric plasma spraying.
summary_en.method: Mo and NiCr 80/20 coatings were deposited on LMD Ti-6Al-4V via APS; microstructural, mechanical, tribological, and corrosion properties were evaluated.
summary_en.result: Mo coatings exhibited the lowest wear rate (0.5×10⁻⁴ mm³/Nm) while NiCr coatings provided superior corrosion resistance with a noble potential of -450 mV.
summary_en.validation: Validated via SEM, EDS, AFM, Vickers microhardness, dry sliding wear tests, and electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5% NaCl.
